findings.title: Service as bounded obligation
findings.claim: The focus commands can be read within the preceding pericope as service that accepts an assigned responsibility, restrains premature release, and remains within the work until its proper completion.
findings.mechanism: The focus Lord title, worship imperative, named worship practice, and intensified endurance meet 19:64's command-controlled movement and denial of forgetfulness. The supplied channel branches connect ownership and completion with devotion, self-restraint, guaranty, and sealing, so worship becomes a bounded responsibility rather than a momentary performance.
findings.reader_payoff: The paired commands make persistence perceptible as a way of keeping an entrusted service intact under the Lord's continuing administration.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains worship Him and persist in His worship. The channel's guaranty and stopper images are bounded semantic relations; the focus is not being translated as a physical seal, a contract, or a claim that every form of patience has this image.

epistemic.reason: The channel support and registered focus facets are trusted, while the contextual administrative contact is supplied as exact Arabic surface evidence without target morphology.

findings.title: The namesake question becomes a creation test

friction_notes: focus_word_alignment resolves all 17 focus words to their QAC identities; no unresolved analysis unit or shared-morpheme collision remains in the supplied bridge.

All eight HFT records have exact focus/context coordinates and complete activation traces. Their legacy_unbound provenance and unresolved context branches are retained as qualification; no branch gloss or facet was invented for those records.

The trusted service candidate and the HFT candidates overlap on worship and endurance carriers but are not exact semantic duplicates: their mechanisms and context changes differ, so each retained candidate owns a dedicated finding.
The native/pericope phase used 19:0 and 19:59-19:76 only. The host basmala produced a bounded naming frame; the 19:69 connection produced a distinct contrast with defiance.

The explicitly added external ayat were quarantined during native/pericope assessment. In the overlay phase, 1:5 supplied a specific worship-plus-help delta and was retained; 1:2 restated the focus's exhaustive Lordship domain, 1:3 lacked a focus carrier, 1:4 repeated the native judgment horizon, and 1:6-1:7 repeated native guidance, deviation, and contrast material, so none added a distinct local finding.

The two outlier candidates remain exploratory: peer-as-visible-mark preserves its split-mapping limitation, and worship-as-roadwork preserves its material-analogy limitation. Neither is presented as a literal lexical replacement.
No additional uncandidate focus branch passed the activation test with a distinct macro change beyond the retained host, native connection, and external overlay findings.
